Caring for a Maltese’s coat takes patience, gentle products, and the right tools. If you keep up with regular brushing and a consistent bath-and-dry routine, you can keep the coat clean, soft, and mostly free of mats and tangles.

1. Gather the correct products and tools.
   Use a high-quality dog shampoo made for long or silky coats, preferably a gentle, moisturizing, tear-free formula. A matching conditioner or leave-in detangling conditioner helps keep the coat slippery and easier to brush. You’ll also want a pin brush, a stainless-steel comb with both wide and fine teeth, a slicker brush for small tangles, a detangling spray, cotton balls for the ears, a non-slip mat or grooming table, absorbent towels, and a blow dryer designed for pets or a human dryer with a cool-to-warm setting.

2. Brush the coat thoroughly before the bath.
   Never bathe a Maltese with tangles still in the coat, because water can tighten knots and turn them into mats. Use a slicker brush to work through the body and legs, then follow with a comb to make sure you can pass through the coat from skin to end. Pay special attention to behind the ears, under the armpits, around the collar area, and the hind legs, since those spots mat fastest.

3. Prepare the dog and bathing area.
   Place cotton balls loosely in the ears to help keep water out, and make sure the tub or wash station has a non-slip surface. Brush out any last-minute tangles before wetting the coat. Have shampoo, conditioner, towels, and the dryer ready so the dog does not have to wait around wet and cold.

4. Wet the coat completely with lukewarm water.
   Soak the coat from neck to tail using gentle water pressure. Keep the face and ears as dry as possible at first, and avoid blasting water directly into sensitive areas. A fully wet coat allows shampoo to spread evenly and reduces the chance of rubbing tangles tighter during washing.

5. Shampoo gently and rinse very well.
   Dilute the shampoo if the label recommends it, then massage it into the coat in the direction of hair growth. Focus on the skin, not just the hair tips, because that is where dirt and oils collect. Rinse thoroughly until the water runs completely clear; leftover shampoo can dry the coat and leave it sticky, which makes matting worse.

6. Apply conditioner or a detangling conditioner.
   Work conditioner through the coat, especially on the longer feathering, legs, and any areas that tangle easily. Let it sit for the recommended time, then rinse well unless you are using a leave-in product. A quality conditioner helps restore slip and makes post-bath brushing much easier.

7. Squeeze out water and towel-dry first.
   Gently press water out of the coat with your hands, then wrap the dog in an absorbent towel. Do not rub hard, since that roughs up the coat and encourages knots. Use a second towel if needed and blot the coat until it is no longer dripping.

8. Blow-dry the coat in sections.
   Start with a pet dryer or a dryer on low heat and low speed, keeping it moving so you do not overheat the skin. As you dry each section, brush it straight with a pin brush and follow with a comb. Drying while brushing is the key to a smooth, fluffy, tangle-free coat on a Maltese.

9. Check for hidden tangles and finish with a comb-through.
   Once the coat is dry, use the stainless-steel comb from skin to ends on the entire body. If the comb catches, go back with the slicker brush and detangling spray on that spot before moving on. Finish by trimming any tiny problem areas if needed and removing the cotton from the ears.

10. Maintain the coat between baths.
    Brush the Maltese several times a week, and ideally daily if the coat is long. Use a light detangling spray before brushing to reduce breakage and help prevent mats. Regular upkeep matters more than any single bath, because a Maltese coat stays healthy and tangle-free only when it is handled consistently.

For the full bath-to-blow-dry process, expect about 1 to 2 hours for a pet with a short, well-kept coat, and 2 to 3 hours or more if the coat is long, the dog is wiggly, or there are tangles that need extra work. The better the coat is maintained between grooming sessions, the faster and easier each bath will be.

In short, a Maltese coat stays beautiful when you combine gentle products, careful drying, and frequent brushing. Stay consistent, and the coat will be much less likely to mat or tangle.
